title: Feet Off
startingPosition: Bottom player lies on back, feet pointed at top player. Top player stands in front.

players.objective: Stay on your feet, keep at least one hand connected to your partner at all times, and keep their feet off of you.
players.winCondition: Continuous - no win condition for top player.
constraints: No chest-to-chest
No double knees down

players.objective: Use hands and feet to connect to top player and make them fall on their butt.
players.winCondition: Butt touches the mat = bottom player wins. Switch top to bottom each time.

constraints: Switch top to bottom every time bottom player wins

title: Inside Position
startingPosition: Bottom player lies on back, feet pointed at top player. Top player stands in front.

players.objective: Same rules as Feet Off, but now also try to get one leg between your partner's knees and keep it there. If it comes out, fight to get it back.
Try to get both feet to the inside of your partner's knees, then use that to make them hit their butt.
players.winCondition: Make top player hit their butt.

title: Cover the Hips
startingPosition: Bottom player lies on back, feet pointed at top player. Top player stands in front.

players.objective: Clear the feet, advance to the knees, then cover/surround your partner's hips with any two parts of your body (hands, knees, elbows).
Same as before - make top player hit their butt.
players.winCondition: Make top player hit their butt.

designRationale: Progression of Feet Off game, adding hip coverage as the terminal win condition.

title: Stay on Top, Hold Them Down
startingPosition: Start chest-to-chest, past the legs.

players.objective: Stay on top and hold your partner down. Move around their body however you like, but don't let them up.
Push top player off and get your legs back in front of them.
players.winCondition: Get legs back in front. Switch when successful.

constraints: Switch when bottom player gets their legs back in front

title: Get Under the Elbows
startingPosition: Start chest-to-chest, past the legs.

players.objective: Stay on top, hold them down AND get one arm underneath your partner's elbows with hands connected.
players.winCondition: One arm under elbows + hands connected = win.

players.objective: Push on top player's hips and knees to create space and get legs back in front.

title: Scalable Pinning (Choose Your Difficulty)
startingPosition: Chest-to-chest, past the legs.

players.objective: Easy: Get one arm under elbows, connect hands. Medium: Get both arms under elbows, connect hands. Hard: Both arms under elbows, connect hands, AND cover the hips.
Create space, get legs back in front or reverse top player.
players.winCondition: Get legs back in front or reverse.

constraints: Players choose their own difficulty level
designRationale: Scaling for mixed-level groups - same game, different win conditions by level.

title: Hands Down / Knee Touch Snapdown Entry
startingPosition: Both players standing, hand fighting.

players.objective: Farm as many points as possible: Make partner's hands touch the mat, touch behind partner's knees, connect hands around partner's body.

designRationale: There's a relationship between the ability to defend legs and defend the head. When the head is low, legs are unavailable. When the head is high, the legs are available. Combining knee touches with hands-down forces the partner to defend the legs by dropping their head and hands into position for a snapdown.

title: Closed Hands Snapdown + Clinch Entry
startingPosition: Both players standing, hand fighting.

players.objective: Two ways to win: Collect 3 points (hands to mat or grip behind knees) OR achieve any closed-hand connection around the partner's head, body, or leg.

constraints: Mix and match focus as you see fit

title: Foot Sweeps — Foot-to-Foot Contact
startingPosition: One player with an underhook, one with an overhook.

players.objective: Keep the overhook at all times. Move the partner around using both hands. Make foot-to-foot contact on either leg, inside or outside.
constraints: Must keep overhook at all times

players.objective: Achieve a closed-hand connection anywhere below the armpits down to the ankles.
players.winCondition: Closed-hand connection. Grabbing the hand does not count.

constraints: On a fall/win: Switch roles, reset.

title: Connection Cycling (Knee / Hip / Ankle)
startingPosition: Single leg connected around the knee pit.

players.objective: Stay connected at all times. Destabilize partner (move them toward hands or hips). Continuously cycle connection between knee to ankle to hip on either leg.
constraints: Stay connected at all times

players.objective: Keep hands on partner (off the mat). Keep partner in front.
players.winCondition: Free all connections and get both feet on the floor.

title: Single Leg Finish
startingPosition: Single leg connected around the knee pit.

players.objective: Takedown (hip or knee touching the mat for 3 seconds). Focus on lifting the ankle as high as possible or double leg control.
players.winCondition: Hip or knee touching mat for 3 seconds.

players.objective: Free yourself of all connections while standing.
players.winCondition: Free of all connections while standing.

title: Dynamic Starts (Finishing the Shot)
startingPosition: Both players moving freely. Attacker begins either with hands behind back or turned around (alternating each round).

players.objective: Finish the back take, then finish the back down pin (chest-to-chest, hips covered), then finish the submission.
players.winCondition: Complete all three objectives in order.

players.objective: Counter: get on top, go behind, or submit. Negate: break all connections once the attack begins.
constraints: May not use hands until attacker makes first connection
Round 1: attacker hands behind back. Round 2: attacker turned around.
designRationale: Dynamic starts lower the barrier to entry — they let the shooter get in deep, which forces the defender to engage once the takedown is imminent rather than before contact is made.

title: Hand Fight: Collect & Connect
startingPosition: Standing, hand fighting (any grip).

players.objective: Collect 3 touches total: partner's hands to the mat, or behind the knee touches. Then land any closed hand connection.
players.winCondition: After collecting 3 touches, land a closed hand connection.

constraints: Resets: Start again each time someone wins.

title: Stay Connected: Put Them Down to Switch
startingPosition: Standing, already connected in one of three positions: front headlock, tight waist, or single leg.

players.objective: Stay continuously connected, cycling between the three connection points. Must get partner's hands to touch the mat before switching connection points.
constraints: Must get partner's hands to mat before switching grips

players.objective: Break the connection and turn to face. If knocked to hip: must get back up.
players.winCondition: Break connection and face. Roles swap on each escape.
constraints: No staying on the floor if knocked to hip
Continuous — defender wins each escape; roles swap on each escape

title: Hand Fighting / Inside Position (Standup)
startingPosition: Both players standing, neutral.

players.objective: Get your elbows inside your partner's elbows and your head on your partner.
players.winCondition: No terminal win condition — continuous warm-up game.

constraints: Bonus: Once inside with head connected, do a shuffle step forward to create urgency

title: Guard Pummeling (Elbows vs. Feet)
startingPosition: One player standing, one player on their back in front of them.

players.objective: Keep elbows inside partner's feet/shins. Work back inside when partner reclaims position.
Keep feet inside top's elbows, push on biceps/shoulders.

title: Takedown to Back Control
startingPosition: Standing, connected (rotate through: single leg, double leg, body lock). Top player takes partner down cooperatively.

players.objective: Keep the bottom player's knees facing the ceiling immediately off the takedown. If the bottom player gets their knees to the mat, score via hooks in, a body triangle, or a guard pass.
Get knees facing the mat as fast as possible, then get to feet or on top to escape.
players.winCondition: Get to feet or on top to escape.

designRationale: Punishing people for bad back takes when they turtle — win conditions force getting on top or to feet.

title: ADCC Simulation Round
startingPosition: Standing, neutral.

players.objective: Score via ADCC rules (takedowns, guard passes, back takes, sweeps). First 1 minute = no points. Final 3 minutes = points active.
players.winCondition: Submission ends the match, or most points after 4 minutes.
constraints: 4-minute round format
First 1 minute = no points. Final 3 minutes = points active.
designRationale: Focus on pacing, risk management, staying disciplined with hand fighting when tired.

title: Down Two Points (Bottom Pressure)
startingPosition: One player on bottom (two-feet-in guard), one player on top. Bottom player is down by 2 points with 2 minutes left.

players.objective: Must score at least 2 points (sweep, takedown) or submit.
constraints: Scenario: down by 2 points with 2 minutes left

players.objective: Maintain position, stay active to avoid stalling calls, protect the lead.

designRationale: Simulates the scenario of being down and on bottom, needing to find a way to get on top.

title: Hand Fighting / Inside Position (Post-Round)
startingPosition: Both players standing, after a hard round (tired).

players.objective: Get inside elbow position with head connected + shuffle step forward.
players.winCondition: Win: inside position with head + shuffle. Lose: partner touches behind your knees, or partner is inside you moving forward.

designRationale: We need to be sharp with hand fights even when tired.

title: Overhook/Underhook — Sticking and Connecting
startingPosition: Standing, clinch — one player has overhook, one has underhook. Neither can remove their hook.

players.objective: Stick feet to partner's feet and follow them. Use the overhook to get partner's hands to touch and stay on the mat.
constraints: Must keep overhook at all times

players.objective: Get hands connected anywhere from under partner's armpits to their ankles.
constraints: Must keep underhook at all times
Neither player can remove their hook

title: Stick and Pull
startingPosition: Standing, overhook/underhook clinch.

players.objective: Stick and pull in any direction to put partner on their butt or back. OR capture partner's head and connect hands around it.
players.winCondition: Two options: put partner down OR capture head with connected hands.

players.objective: Precursor: get hands connected first. Then split and twist (step between legs and twist to back) OR block and lift (block a leg and lift).
players.winCondition: Put partner on butt/back. Roles switch.

constraints: Win → roles switch

title: Upper vs. Lower Body
startingPosition: Standing, free movement.

players.objective: Get connected to a leg, then either: get out to the ankle and put it in the armpit, OR get connected to the hips then lift both feet off ground OR get behind.
Can only connect hips-to-arms or hips-to-shoulders — no touching legs.
players.winCondition: Must put partner on their butt or back.
constraints: No touching legs
Win → roles switch

title: Get to the Back
startingPosition: Both players standing.

players.objective: Try to get behind your partner.

constraints: Continuous

title: Frame Game (1-1-2 format)
startingPosition: Standing.

players.objective: Get hands connected around partner's leg or trunk (single leg or body lock).
Use frames to prevent attacker's hands from connecting.

constraints: Format: One side attacks, then the other, then both

title: Over-Under Disconnect
startingPosition: Over-under clinch.

players.objective: From over-under, reach single leg or body lock.
Break to neutrality.

constraints: Flip-flop roles on each point

title: Back → Single → Back (Continuous)
startingPosition: Back body lock.

players.objective: Start from back body lock, go to single leg, return to back — repeat as long as possible.
Escape to neutrality.

title: Two-on-One to Single
startingPosition: Standing.

players.objective: Establish a two-on-one, convert to single leg.
Break out / maintain neutrality.

constraints: Tip: The closer the leg is to the arm, the better

title: Catch and Release Wrestling (Closing)
startingPosition: Both players standing.

players.objective: Full standup wrestling, no takedowns to the floor.
constraints: No takedowns to the floor
Multiple rounds, new partner each time

title: Have More Grips Than Them
startingPosition: Both players standing, handfighting.

players.objective: Have more grips on your partner than they have on you.
constraints: Can only grip from wrist to armpit
Can only grip from wrist to armpit

title: Completing the Full Pin — Side
source: Greg Souders Seminar Session 1 (10th Planet South Bay)
startingPosition: Partner on their side. Top player hands connected around partner's waist.

players.objective: Achieve in any order: chest-to-chest or chest-to-back contact, get under both elbows with connected hands, cover the hips.
Escape via any of three options.
players.winCondition: Get both legs back in front, OR roll top player over, OR stand up.

title: Segmentation to Pin
source: Greg Souders Seminar Session 1 (10th Planet South Bay)
startingPosition: Partner on their side. Top player hands connected around partner's waist.

players.objective: In sequence: remove partner's hands, get under or behind the elbows, connect to shoulders and cover hips.
players.winCondition: Same as Completing the Full Pin.

players.objective: Same three options as Full Pin game.
players.winCondition: Get both legs back in front, roll top player over, or stand up.

designRationale: Segmenting the periphery sequentially: hands → elbows → shoulders.

title: Standing to Locked Hands
source: Greg Souders Seminar Session 1 (10th Planet South Bay)
startingPosition: Top player standing with one leg between partner's knees, hands on partner's stomach. Bottom player supine.

players.objective: Stay on top and hold partner down. Connect hands around partner's hips or shoulders in any closed-hand connection.
players.winCondition: Connected hands around hips or shoulders.

players.objective: Make top player hit their butt.

title: Denying the Feet — Fully Disconnected
source: Greg Souders Seminar Session 1 (10th Planet South Bay)
startingPosition: Top player completely disconnected and standing in front of partner's legs. Bottom player supine.

players.objective: Keep partner's feet off of you. Step between or outside partner's knees. Connect hands around hips or shoulders. Hold partner down throughout.
players.winCondition: Connected hands around hips or shoulders.

players.objective: Connect with hands and feet on top player, or make top player hit their butt.
players.winCondition: Connect hands and feet, OR butt hit.

title: Full Process — Seated Start
source: Greg Souders Seminar Session 1 (10th Planet South Bay)
startingPosition: Partner seated. Top player standing, disconnected.

players.objective: Put partner on their back or get behind them. Then: chest-to-chest or chest-to-back contact, connected hands around shoulders, and hips covered.
Make top player hit their butt, or stand up and connect around top player's body while standing.

title: Clearing Frames (Wrist Pin Passing)
source: CLA Wrist Pin Guard Passing @ Enso Jiu-Jitsu Seminar
startingPosition: Half guard. Bottom player on their side, both hands on top player's chest. Top player leaning in. No knees as frames allowed for bottom player.

players.objective: Pin one of bottom player's wrists to their own hip. Get your own other arm across the body and make chest-to-chest contact.
constraints: May not pass through the legs

players.objective: Keep frames extended to hold top player away.
constraints: Must keep half guard closed
No knees as frames
Top player may not pass through the legs
Bottom player must keep half guard closed

title: Getting Under Elbows (Wrist Pin Passing)
source: CLA Wrist Pin Guard Passing @ Enso Jiu-Jitsu Seminar
startingPosition: Same as Clearing Frames, but top player starts with one wrist already pinned to hip and own other arm across the body.

players.objective: Maintain wrist pin while getting under at least one elbow and connecting hands.
Two options: get both feet back to the middle of partner's knees, OR use knees to make top player fall over.

constraints: Alternate which wrist is controlled each round

title: Clearing the Knee (Wrist Pin Passing)
source: CLA Wrist Pin Guard Passing @ Enso Jiu-Jitsu Seminar
startingPosition: Top player has one knee cutting through, bottom player's both knees in front. No hands on each other.

players.objective: Control wrists and cover hips, then use any opportunity to get under at least one elbow, get chest-to-chest, and lock hands.
constraints: May stand up if wrist control is maintained

players.objective: Put top player on their butt AND get both feet inside holding both ankles.

designRationale: Combines wrist control with leg entry — half guard / open guard transition.

title: Standing vs. Supine — Knee Line Control (Progression A)
startingPosition: Bottom player on back. Top player standing, starting with hands on partner's feet, in front of the feet.

players.objective: Move feet out of the way and advance to the line of the knees (inside or outside). Hold partner down from that position.
constraints: Cannot lower chest to chest contact
Cannot put both knees on the floor

players.objective: Three wins: sit up off the back, get both feet inside partner's legs and maintain it, or make top player's butt hit the floor.

title: Standing vs. Supine — Outside Knee Line (Progression B)
startingPosition: Top player already at knee line, outside partner's legs. Hands on partner's feet.

players.objective: Same as Progression A but must specifically maintain position outside partner's legs. Focus on pulling their head close to negate leg pummeling.
constraints: No chest-to-chest
No knees on floor

players.objective: Three wins: get both feet back in front and connected to top player, get both feet inside partner's legs, or make top player's butt/back hit floor.
constraints: No leg entanglements — open foot connections only
Cannot commit all attachments to one leg
No leg entanglements — open foot connections only (posts, hooks)
Cannot commit all attachments to one leg

title: Line Holding
startingPosition: Bottom player supine, top player past the feet (shin on same-side hamstring or outside past feet).

players.objective: Maintain position past the feet for the whole round.
constraints: Cannot put knees down
Cannot go chest-to-chest (chest-to-back allowed)

players.objective: Make top player's hip touch the mat, or get up to feet.

designRationale: If the bottom player made your hip touch, that means their feet were on you somehow.

title: Staying Behind the Knees (Double Under)
source: CLA Double Under Passing @ Next Level MMA
startingPosition: Top player with both arms under partner's knees, hands open. Bottom player in guard.

players.objective: Keep at least one arm behind the partner's knees at all times. Can play anywhere hip to hip, open or closed hands.
constraints: Keep at least one arm behind knees at all times

players.objective: Three ways to win: get both feet to the inside of the top player's arms or legs, make a closed leg connection around top player's shoulders, or sit up and push away disconnecting completely.

designRationale: Double unders chosen over single because the margin between staying engaged and losing the position is wider — you can transition between double and single while remaining in the task.

title: Connecting Hands Past the Hips or Shoulders (Double Under)
source: CLA Double Under Passing @ Next Level MMA
startingPosition: Same as Staying Behind the Knees — top player with both arms under partner's knees, hands open.

players.objective: Maintain at least one arm behind a knee while working. Connect hands past the partner's legs — around hips or shoulders, any facing.
players.winCondition: Hands connected past the legs. Flipping the partner over counts.

players.objective: Same three win conditions as Staying Behind the Knees.
players.winCondition: Feet inside, closed leg connection around shoulders, or sit up and disconnect.

designRationale: Hips and shoulders are strong points of connection that manage rotation. In positions where rotation is possible, connecting there stops the bottom player from moving.

title: Getting to the Knees from Standing (Double Under)
source: CLA Double Under Passing @ Next Level MMA
startingPosition: Top player standing behind partner's feet. Bottom player on back.

players.objective: Keep the partner's feet in front while working any part of the body behind the partner's knee pits. Once behind the knees: connect hands past the legs at hips or shoulders.
players.winCondition: Same finish as Connecting Hands game.

players.objective: Three ways to win: get both feet to the inside, trap top player's shoulders with legs, or sit up and away disconnecting.

constraints: Feet-to-inside-the-biceps removed as win condition at this distance
designRationale: Feet-to-inside-the-biceps removed as a win condition because at this starting distance it becomes the obvious go-to solution and would shortcut the intended experience.

title: Open Guard: Pass the Outsides
startingPosition: Bottom player belly up in open guard, top player standing.

players.objective: Precursor: get to the outside of one side, then the other, then back to the first (alternating L-R-L or R-L-R). Then close hands anywhere from hips to shoulders.
constraints: Must alternate sides

players.objective: Make top player's butt touch the mat, OR get up and wrestle into any close hand connection.

title: Open Guard: Pass the Insides
startingPosition: Same as Pass the Outsides — belly up open guard, top player standing.

players.objective: Precursor: get between partner's feet and contact either knee pit with one leg, then the other, then once more (alternating, 3 total). Then close hands from waist to shoulders.
Same as Pass the Outsides — put top player on their butt, or get up into a close hand connection.

title: Denying Supine Guard (from Seated)
startingPosition: Bottom player seated guard against standing passer.

players.objective: Avoid getting put on your back. Standing up and freeing yourself from any connection. Destabilise your partner to their butt or both hands touching the mat.
players.winCondition: Stand up free, or destabilise partner.
constraints: You lose if you are on your back without an established guard

players.objective: Stay standing. Put the guard player on his back without an established guard.
players.winCondition: Put guard player on back without established guard.

title: Destabilising or Wrestling Up from Seated Guard
startingPosition: Bottom player seated guard against standing passer. Difficulty can be changed by starting with grips in place.

players.objective: Destabilise partner to their butt or both hands touching the mat. OR wrestle up to a strong closed hand connection with both standing.
Stay standing. Get to the outside of the bottom player's legs and stay there for as long as possible.

constraints: Difficulty can be changed by starting with grips in place

title: Wrestling Up from Connection
startingPosition: One player seated, one player standing.

players.objective: 1st priority: keep top player's hands off of you. 2nd priority: make leg-to-leg connections. Win: go belly up to destabilize → achieve hip entanglement OR get partner's hands to mat. OR wrestle up from connection to partner's hips.
players.winCondition: Either win condition. Both destabilization and entanglement must be present.
constraints: Must establish connection to a leg first

players.objective: Work to the outside of the legs, put bottom player on their back.
players.winCondition: Achieve shin-to-body contact anywhere from hips to shoulders.

designRationale: Starting with just the connection-and-destabilize task can be isolated before adding wrestle ups and entanglements.

title: Seated Handfight
startingPosition: Top player standing/kneeling, bottom player seated.

players.objective: Connect hands around bottom player's upper body (headlock, body lock), OR make both shoulders touch the mat.
players.winCondition: Either option. Top player wins = flip roles.

players.objective: Prevent top player from connecting. Stay seated.
constraints: Cannot stand
Cannot sweep
No closed fists
Bottom player cannot stand or sweep

title: Guard Retention — Stay Connected
source: Supine Open Guard Series (Black Flag Jiu-Jitsu Seminar)
startingPosition: Bottom player on back, both hooks between partner's knees, one hand on each ankle. Top player standing.

players.objective: Keep tops or bottoms of feet touching partner anywhere. Keep hands connected. Push/pull partner with feet freely.
Get both legs to the outside of bottom player's legs with all connections broken.
players.winCondition: Both legs outside + all connections broken.

constraints: Change top/bottom every time top player wins

title: Competing Destabilizations
source: Supine Open Guard Series (Black Flag Jiu-Jitsu Seminar)
startingPosition: Same as Guard Retention.

players.objective: Cause 3 total destabilizations: the partner's hands touch the mat, initiated by the bottom player, OR the partner's butt touches the mat.
Get outside the legs 3 times, alternating sides. Each time: both feet outside and touch partner's body with shin.
constraints: Must alternate sides — cannot repeat same side consecutively
Whoever hits 3 conditions first wins.

title: Guard to Hip Control
source: Supine Open Guard Series (Black Flag Jiu-Jitsu Seminar)
startingPosition: Same as Guard Retention.

players.objective: Wrestle up to standing, OR push partner to butt AND get hands connected around their hips.
Clear the feet (inside or outside) and lock hands around partner's hips/waist.
players.winCondition: Clear feet + lock hands around hips/waist.

constraints: Change top/bottom every time someone wins

title: Inside Position vs. Leg Entanglement
source: Supine Open Guard Series (Black Flag Jiu-Jitsu Seminar)
startingPosition: Bottom player on back with feet between partner's legs and hands on partner's ankles. Top player standing.

players.objective: Entangle one leg, then disentangle and entangle the other.
Get both feet to the inside of bottom player's legs at any time.

constraints: Change top/bottom every time someone wins

title: Butterfly Guard — Inside/Outside Position
startingPosition: Alternating each turn: both feet inside, OR one foot inside, one outside with a hand on the ankle.

players.objective: Use feet and hands in any orientation to get partner's butt to hit the mat.
Get both legs to the outside of partner's feet and touch shin to their body.
players.winCondition: Shin touches partner's body with both legs outside.

designRationale: If the conditions for a technique are not present, the effect cannot happen. This game trains the conditions that make butterfly sweeps possible.

title: Knee Shield Half Guard: Destabilize
startingPosition: Knee shield half guard — bottom player's knee between them and the top player. Two legs interacting with one.

players.objective: Use connections (hands, knees, feet) to make top player's hands or hips touch the mat.
constraints: Must stay in half guard — two legs interacting with one

players.objective: Make chest-to-chest or chest-to-back contact.

designRationale: If your head is high your legs are available, if your head is low you are easier to snap down. Getting close immobilizes the bottom player.

title: Knee Shield Half Guard: Feet to the Inside
startingPosition: Same as Knee Shield Destabilize.

players.objective: Destabilize (hands or hips to mat). During destabilization, get both feet to the inside of top player's knees.
Chest-to-chest or chest-to-back contact.

title: Knee Shield Half Guard: Full Entanglement
startingPosition: Same as Knee Shield Destabilize.

players.objective: Destabilize. Get feet to the inside. Connect both legs to opponent's hips (inside, outside, or mixed).
players.winCondition: Attached to hips with both legs.

players.objective: Chest-to-chest or chest-to-back contact.

designRationale: All entanglements rely on inside positioning — inside position gives access to the hips.

title: Segmenting to Pin (Half Guard)
startingPosition: Half guard / top player already past the knees, bottom player framing.

players.objective: Close connection at the shoulders (under one or both arms) AND past the legs — mount, side body, back mount all count.
constraints: Must stay ahead of each line — feet → knees → hips → hands/elbows → shoulders

players.objective: Three options to win.
players.winCondition: Top player's hip touches mat, OR get up to feet, OR re-establish closed guard.

constraints: Top player must stay ahead of each line
designRationale: Don't think side control or mount — think about what's directly in front of you and remove it.

title: K-Guard: Getting Inside Position
source: CLA Guard Games @ Team Laurien and Alex
startingPosition: Bottom player supine, both feet outside partner's hips, one hand gripping partner's knee. Top player standing.

players.objective: Get feet inside and grip both ankles, either front-facing or rear-facing. Put the partner on the ground. The inside-position and put-down conditions may be completed in any order; only then finish any entanglement.
players.winCondition: Inside position + put partner down + entanglement.

players.objective: Stay standing at all times. Keep hands on partner. Stay on the outside of the bottom player's legs, foot to foot.
constraints: If you fall to knees, stand back up

designRationale: Destabilisation is required before entanglement for two reasons. First, more time in position = more opportunity to recognise what's available. Second, safety — entanglements produce force through rotation, which is where beginners get hurt against standing players.

title: DLR (vs. Standing)
source: CLA Guard Games @ Team Laurien and Alex
startingPosition: Bottom player supine with one cross hook and same-side grip on the ankle. Top player standing.

players.objective: Get feet inside and grip both ankles, either front-facing or rear-facing. Put the partner on the ground. The inside-position and put-down conditions may be completed in any order; only then finish any entanglement.
Stay standing. Stay on the outside of the bottom player's legs for as long as possible.

designRationale: Same as K-Guard game but from a more constrained start.

title: Putting It All Together (from Closed Guard)
source: CLA Guard Games @ Team Laurien and Alex
startingPosition: Closed guard.

players.objective: Three ways to win: grip under elbow + closed-hand connection to shoulder/head; shoulder connection with head covered or arm pulled out; any entanglement (partner grounded first).
Get to feet, open the guard, and reach the outside of the bottom player's legs.
players.winCondition: Touch the bottom player's body anywhere with the shin.

constraints: Players choose their own focus
designRationale: Multiple win conditions reflecting the full range of connections explored.

title: Stay Connected (Bottom Player Exploration)
startingPosition: Bottom player on back/seated, top player in front.

players.objective: Keep hands connected at all times. Hold partner as close as possible.
Put both hands on partner's chest and push away.
players.winCondition: Achieve separation (head to chest, grips broken open).

title: Connected Clinch — Put Partner on Back
startingPosition: Same as Stay Connected, alternating between head and arm connection, both hands around shoulder.

players.objective: Put partner on their back or get on top / behind partner.
players.winCondition: Partner on back or you on top/behind.
constraints: Only the given connections are allowed
Highly constrained — only the given connections are allowed
designRationale: Designed as discovery: Trial to trial until you understand the things that let you be successful or fail.

title: Arm/Wrist Control — Cause Posting
startingPosition: Bottom player on back, top player above.

players.objective: Grip focus: partner's wrists, elbows, and hands. Cause posting → get hands connected → get behind, on top, or put partner on back.
players.winCondition: Behind, on top, or partner on back.

players.objective: Connect hands around partner.
players.winCondition: Put bottom player on their back or go around the legs.
constraints: Cannot stand up on both feet — one foot only
Top player cannot stand up on both feet — one foot only

title: Head & Arm Trap — Ankle Cross
startingPosition: Bottom player on back with partner's head and arm trapped between crossed ankles.

players.objective: Keep feet crossed (ankles only). Use hands to keep partner close.
players.winCondition: Keep feet crossed AND arm trapped.
constraints: Ankles only — no locking into bend of knee

players.objective: Pull arm out or separate partner's feet.

title: Overhook Escape
startingPosition: Bottom player with overhook connection, top player trapped.

players.objective: Keep body down, arms separated. Get head and arm fastened together (completing the overhook trap).
Put both hands on partner's chest and free the arm from the overhook.
players.winCondition: Both conditions must be met to win.

title: Hips to Shoulders (Crab Ride Progression)
startingPosition: Crab ride (top player feet inside behind knees, partner facing away).

players.objective: First destabilize to hands or hips touching mat, then advance to hips. From hips: destabilize again, then advance to shoulders.
constraints: Must make hands or hips touch before progressing to each line

players.objective: Return to seated guard or get to standing neutral.

constraints: Two-stage destabilization required
designRationale: You must make the hands touch or hips touch before you go to the hips. Then once at hips, must destabilize again before shoulders.

title: Stay Behind / Back Control Entry (Turtle)
startingPosition: Defender on hands and knees. Attacker chest-to-back, hands connected around defender's shoulders.

players.objective: Stay behind both of defender's elbows at all times. Keep defender between your limbs. Drive defender's hands to the mat.
constraints: One hook allowed at a time — both hooks simultaneously prohibited

players.objective: Stand up and get both hands off the mat, OR turn to face the attacker.

constraints: One hook allowed at a time — both hooks simultaneously prohibited

title: Holding Under the Elbows — Mount
source: Greg Souders Seminar Session 1 (10th Planet South Bay)
startingPosition: Mount. Top player with double underhooks, hands connected.

players.objective: Stay on top, keep hips and shoulders covered, maintain arms under both partner's elbows.
Get both elbows back to touch their own body, or make top player fall off.

title: Getting Under the Elbows — Mount
source: Greg Souders Seminar Session 1 (10th Planet South Bay)
startingPosition: Mount. Hips and shoulders covered, but no underhooks.

players.objective: Keep hips and shoulders covered and chest contact throughout. Get both arms under partner's elbows and connect hands.
players.winCondition: Both arms under elbows + hands connected.

players.objective: Push on partner's hips and knees to get own knees back in front, or make top player fall off.

title: Stopping Rotation — Back Mount
source: Greg Souders Seminar Session 1 (10th Planet South Bay)
startingPosition: Chest-to-back. One arm over, one arm under partner's shoulder. No hooks allowed.

players.objective: Keep chest-to-back contact no matter where partner goes.
constraints: No hooks — legs can go anywhere on back side of body only

players.objective: Remove partner's connections and turn to face.

constraints: No hooks allowed

title: Get Under the Elbow (B-Team Day 1)
startingPosition: Top player past the legs, hands locked around partner's hips, chest-to-chest, same side.

players.objective: Get at least one arm underneath one of partner's elbows. Lock hands around partner's shoulders.
players.winCondition: One arm under elbow + hands locked around shoulders.

players.objective: Get back off the mat — sit up, stand up, or reverse.

title: Stay Under the Elbows, Submit (B-Team Day 1)
startingPosition: Top player with double underhooks under partner's elbows, hips covered.

players.objective: Stay under at least one elbow at all times. Submit partner — only while under at least one elbow.
players.winCondition: Submit while under at least one elbow.
constraints: Both elbows touch body simultaneously = top player loses

players.objective: Bring both elbows to body to make top player lose.
players.winCondition: Both elbows to body = instant win.

constraints: All submissions must be executed from underneath the elbow

title: Hips to Shoulders (10th Planet South Bay)
source: 10th Planet South Bay Full CLA Practice
startingPosition: Floor — top player hands locked under partner's hips. Three alternating setups.

players.objective: Move from hips connection to shoulders connection. Must get under at least one elbow and lock hands.
Separate top player's hands, then: sit up, reverse, or stand up.

constraints: Three alternating starting setups
designRationale: When we let go of the hips to go to the shoulders, we become vulnerable to movement and space.

title: Submitting While Under Elbows (10th Planet South Bay)
source: 10th Planet South Bay Full CLA Practice
startingPosition: Floor — chest-to-chest or chest-to-back, under at least one elbow.

players.objective: Must submit partner. Must maintain something under at least one elbow at all times.
constraints: Lose position under both elbows = instant loss

players.objective: Get both elbows touching their own body with nothing underneath.
players.winCondition: Both elbows to body = instant win.

constraints: Hands, head, leg, figure-four grips all count as being under the elbow
designRationale: By forcing you to stay under at least one elbow, we're always forcing you to interact with the arm and neck together.

title: Mount — Under Elbow Control to Submission
startingPosition: Mount. Top player starts with underhooks. Bottom player actively resisting.

players.objective: Stay on top, hold down. Must remain under or behind at least one elbow. Head and arm must be bound before submitting.
constraints: Must have head and arm bound before submitting
Losing both elbows = automatic loss

players.objective: Free your elbows and/or escape back control.

constraints: Back control with hooks/body triangle counts as under elbows

title: Mount — No Grips to Submission
startingPosition: Mount. Bottom player starts with forearm across the hip frame.

players.objective: Stay on top, hold down. Must have head and arm bound together before any submission attempt.
constraints: Head and arm must be bound before submitting

players.objective: Get feet in front (to guard) or reverse.

title: Holding the Breaking Position
startingPosition: Armbar breaking position — one leg over head, one under armpit. Any connection.

players.objective: Stay as close to partner's shoulder as possible and hold them to the floor.
Pull arm free from top player's legs, or get back off the mat.

title: Holding from Above the Shoulder
startingPosition: From armbar position, tuck shin behind partner's head, transition body on top and base on the other side.

players.objective: Stay on top, stay close to shoulder, hold partner to the floor.
Pull arm free, or make top player hit their back.

title: Holding from Mount
startingPosition: Mount with double underhooks, hands connected.

players.objective: Stay on top, hold partner down, keep arms under partner's elbows.
Pull elbows in to touch their own body, or make top player fall off.

title: Isolating the Arm — Breaking Position
startingPosition: Armbar breaking position. Any connection.

players.objective: Stay on top, hold partner down, and separate partner's hands — keep them separated.
Pull arm free, or make top player fall over. Try to reconnect hands.

title: Isolating the Arm — From Above the Shoulder
startingPosition: Same transition as Holding from Above the Shoulder.

players.objective: Stay on top, hold partner down. Cover partner's head and transition to armbar breaking position. Separate and isolate the arm.
Pull arm free, get back off mat, or get on top. Try to reconnect hands.

title: Full Process from Mount
startingPosition: Mount with double underhooks, hands connected.

players.objective: Stay on top using underhooks. Choose one arm, get your whole body behind both elbows. Trap both arms. Cover head and reach armbar breaking position.
Free both arms so both elbows touch their own body, or make top player fall off.

title: Arm Retention Hold-Down
startingPosition: Top player has elbow-to-elbow grip on bottom player's nearest arm. Bottom player on back.

players.objective: Stay attached to the arm. Use legs to hold partner to the floor.
players.winCondition: Maintain arm control AND keep bottom player from reaching knees.

players.objective: Pull arm free OR get up to knees.
players.winCondition: Get to knees (even if top still has the arm).

constraints: Switch roles each time bottom player wins

title: Arm Lock Finish
startingPosition: Same elbow-to-elbow grip, bottom player on back.

players.objective: Stay attached to arm, hold partner down with legs. Once disconnection occurs, straighten the arm to tap.
Pull arm free OR get to knees.
players.winCondition: Pull arm free or get to knees.

designRationale: Progression from Arm Retention Hold-Down — same hold-down, now with submission.

title: Mount Elbow Control — Armbar Setup
startingPosition: Top player mounted, both arms under bottom player's elbows.

players.objective: Keep at least one arm/body part under an elbow. Move one arm out of the way, get entire body behind it, clamp legs onto shoulder.
constraints: Cannot lose position under the elbows

players.objective: Bring both elbows to the mat AND to the body simultaneously.
players.winCondition: Back of arms touching mat + inside of arms touching body.

designRationale: Getting under the elbows is the precondition for the armbar breaking position.

title: Arm Trap Survival
source: Back Control — Arm Trap Series (Black Flag Jiu-Jitsu Seminar)
startingPosition: Attacker chest glued to defender's back. Overarm and underarm grip defender's wrists. Underarm-side leg traps the arm. Feet crossed.

players.objective: Keep chest glued to partner's back. Keep the arm trapped between the feet.
Free the trapped arm OR put back on the mat (breaking chest contact).

constraints: Change top/bottom every time defender wins

title: Arm Trap — Finish It
source: Back Control — Arm Trap Series (Black Flag Jiu-Jitsu Seminar)
startingPosition: Same as Arm Trap Survival.

players.objective: Cross feet into partner's knee pit OR lock up the rear strangle grip (grip only, no finish required).
Free the arm OR put back on the mat.

constraints: Change top/bottom every time someone wins
designRationale: When on someone's back, arms have to stay attached AND threaten/submit. By getting legs involved and trapping arms, we can use our arms differently.

title: Back Control, No Submissions
startingPosition: Back control, seated with defensive grips seatbelt and hooks.

players.objective: Keep chest glued to partner's back.
Break chest-to-chest contact.

title: Back Control with Submissions
startingPosition: Back control, seated with defensive grips seatbelt and hooks.

players.objective: Win by submission. Must be on the back or have a submission threat ongoing.
Break chest-to-chest contact and be free of submission threat.
players.winCondition: Break contact + free of submission threat.

title: Front Headlock — Back to Mat
startingPosition: Front headlock — attacker has hands locked around partner's head and arm. Defender on all fours.

players.objective: Keep hands connected and partner's hands on the mat. Get partner's back to touch the mat while maintaining head and arm connection.
players.winCondition: Back touches mat with connection maintained.

players.objective: Separate the connection and free your head by any means.

title: Front Headlock — Finishing Grip + Hip Cover
startingPosition: Same as Back to Mat — front headlock, defender on all fours.

players.objective: Three conditions in any order: put partner on back, achieve grip (hands behind far shoulder OR wrist into elbow crease), cover partner's hips with legs.
Separate the connection and free your head at any point.

constraints: All three conditions can be achieved in any order
designRationale: Putting partner on back limits mobility. Getting arm toward centerline brings shoulder closer to neck, creating compression. Covering hips immobilizes and adds squeeze.

title: Open Hands / Hands on Mat (Front Headlock Progression 1)
startingPosition: Front headlock — top player has one hand under bottom player's chin, other hand on opposite side.

players.objective: Keep hands open. Keep opponent's hands on the mat. Stay in front.
players.winCondition: No terminal win condition — continuous task.
constraints: Keep hands open
Stay in front — cannot go behind

players.objective: Get to feet, take hands off the mat, pull head free.
players.winCondition: Clear head and get to feet.

title: Close Hands / Head & Arm Trap / Back to Mat (Front Headlock Progression 2)
startingPosition: Same as Progression 1.

players.objective: Three layered tasks: 1) keep hands on mat, 2) close hands and trap head and arm, 3) make back touch mat.
players.winCondition: Back touches mat with hands connected.

players.objective: Stand up and disconnect.

title: Get Behind the Elbow / Arm-In Strangle (Front Headlock Progression 3)
startingPosition: Same as Progression 2.

players.objective: Full task stack: hold hands down → connect hands → put on back → get behind trapped arm's elbow → squeeze.
Stand up, disconnect, or escape.
players.winCondition: Stand up and disconnect, or escape.

designRationale: Game 3 guides toward arm-in strangle variations. 'Naked' strangles have nothing between mechanism and neck. 'Arm-in' includes the arm in the compression.

title: Keeping the Arm Bent (Kimura)
startingPosition: Defending player laying on side with hands locked. Attacking player sitting on defender's head holding kimura grip.

players.objective: Keep the arm bent using the kimura grip.
Straighten and free the arm.

constraints: Task focus: Separate the bent arm from the rest of the body

title: Attack from Kimura Grip
startingPosition: Defending player laying on side with hands locked. Attacking player sitting on defender's head holding kimura grip.

players.objective: Submit while arm is exposed (kimura, armbar, triangle, etc.) or take the back.
Free the arm.

constraints: Safety: don't rip the kimura — people have different shoulder flexibility

title: Finish or Backtake (Leg Drag)
startingPosition: Leg drag (top player has leg across, no chest-to-chest).

players.objective: Finishing on the leg (inside heel hook emphasis) OR taking the back.
players.winCondition: Finish on leg or take back.
constraints: No chest-to-chest

players.objective: Breaking free, OR getting to guard, standing, or getting on top.

constraints: If the back's not there, go right back to the legs
designRationale: Chase hips and hands — alternate between back and legs fluidly. Play the whole space.

title: Triangle — Threat (Lock Setup)
startingPosition: Top player double knees down, legs around partner, one arm in/one arm out.

players.objective: Lock foot into the bend of either knee pit, as close as possible.
constraints: Cannot stand up — must stay double knees down

players.objective: Pull the trapped arm out OR push the free arm back in.

designRationale: Ryan Hall broke triangles into four conditions: threat, lock, angle, finish. Submissions are low-variability.

title: Triangle — Full Finish
startingPosition: Same as Triangle Threat — one arm in, one arm out, top player double knees down.

players.objective: Precursor: keep partner close → lock foot to knee pit → hook under one limb → squeeze to finish.
Pull arm out or put both arms back in.

designRationale: Progression from threat → lock → angle → finish.

title: Straight Ashi — Inside or Outside to Inside Heel Hook
startingPosition: Straight ashi garami with an ankle grip.

players.objective: Get feet to inside or outside position first. Then transition to inside heel hook grip. Then get outside heel hook grip.

title: Inside Position to Inside Heel Hook — No Releasing the Ankles
startingPosition: Seated with both feet on the inside hooking behind partner's knees, ankle grip on both legs.

players.objective: Entangle to outside ashi or SLX — without releasing ankle grips. Get outside heel grip. Then transition to inside heel hook grip.
constraints: Without releasing the ankle grips
Without releasing the ankle grips

title: Outside Heel Grip vs. 2-on-1
startingPosition: Attacker has outside position with a heel grip. Defender has a 2-on-1 grip on the attacker's arm.

players.objective: Submit the partner.
Free yourself of all connections.

title: Ankle Lock and Heel Hook Dilemma
startingPosition: Attacker in SLX with an ankle grip.

players.objective: Point and drive partner's knee down. Submit with ankle lock, or transition to heel grip and submit.
Separate the attacker's connection and free yourself.

title: Supine Inside Position — Entry to Outside or SLX (vs. Standing)
startingPosition: Bottom player supine with both feet inside hooking behind partner's knees, one ankle grip. Top player standing outside.

players.objective: Destabilise the top player and entangle to outside ashi or SLX with a heel hook grip.
constraints: If inside position is lost, regain it before continuing

players.objective: Stay standing and stay on the outside of the partner's legs.

title: Supine Inside Position — Entry vs. Seated Outside Recovery
startingPosition: Bottom player supine with both feet inside, one ankle grip. Top player starts standing outside.

players.objective: Destabilise and entangle to outside ashi or SLX with a heel hook grip.
Get one leg to the outside with the other in a kneebar position, or both legs to the outside.
constraints: If put on butt, must remain seated and work to regain inside position

title: Inside Position — Learning Entanglements (Beginner)
source: Leg Entanglements for Beginners (Greg Souders CLA Seminar)
startingPosition: Straight ashi double seated.

players.objective: In order: get both feet to outside, move partner's leg to other side of body, get both feet back inside.
Separate partner's feet and get both feet between partner's knees.

constraints: Safety: Defender may not rotate to free the leg; must separate feet first then pull straight back
No standing up (for new players)

title: Switching Legs — Chaining Entanglements (Beginner)
source: Leg Entanglements for Beginners (Greg Souders CLA Seminar)
startingPosition: Bottom player on inside with both feet inside, holding both ankles.

players.objective: Entangle one leg, then entangle the other.
Get both feet to the inside at any point before bottom player wins.

title: Destabilising to Entangle (vs. Standing) (Beginner)
source: Leg Entanglements for Beginners (Greg Souders CLA Seminar)
startingPosition: Bottom player supine, both feet between partner's knees, one hand on an ankle. Top player standing.

players.objective: Keep at least one foot inside the partner's legs at all times. Use the tops and bottoms of the feet only to destabilise and bring the partner down—no entangling while standing. Once the partner is down, entangle any leg to win.
players.winCondition: Entangle any leg after partner is down.
constraints: No entangling while standing

players.objective: Get both legs to the outside. Touch shin from hips to shoulders.
players.winCondition: Shin touch from hips to shoulders.
constraints: If you fall, must regain inside from ground
Safety: Defender may not rotate to pull the leg out; must separate feet first then pull straight back

title: Inside Position vs. Standing Passer (Diego Pato)
source: How to Defeat Diego Pato (Deandre Corbe's Training)
startingPosition: Bottom player supine, top player standing.

players.objective: Get both feet hooked inside the top player's knees, from ankle to hip. Maintain a two-hand connection to both legs. Put the top player on their butt.

Keep one leg between the bottom player's knees at all times. Keep the outside leg from crossing to the inside—step inside or outside, and stay right in front. Never let both feet reach the inside simultaneously: one is fine; two is bad.
constraints: Never let both feet reach the inside simultaneously

title: Inside Position + Cross Leg + Path to Top (Diego Pato)
source: How to Defeat Diego Pato (Deandre Corbe's Training)
startingPosition: Double seated leg drag.

players.objective: Keep both feet inside the partner's legs at all times. Maintain a two-hand connection to both legs. Continuously toggle between cross leg and straight leg, keeping feet hidden inside. Keep the partner grounded; the full space may be played, from seated to standing.
Get to their feet and get one leg to the inside; order doesn't matter.

title: Inside Position + Cross Leg + Hip Access (Diego Pato)
source: How to Defeat Diego Pato (Deandre Corbe's Training)
startingPosition: Double seated leg drag.

players.objective: Entangle — connect legs to hips keeping them grounded, OR come up — gain access to hips by closing hands keeping them grounded.
Get to feet AND get one leg to the inside.

designRationale: Gaining access to partner's center is central to almost all things. Both legs and arms need a path to center.

title: Entanglement Flow (SLX ↔ Outside Entanglement)
startingPosition: Both seated, attacker in Single Leg X.

players.objective: Switch from SLX → Outside Entanglement → back to SLX. Then switch to other leg and repeat.
constraints: Must maintain connection throughout

players.objective: Break all connections and free the leg.

constraints: Swap roles each round

title: Three-Condition Leg Control (B-Team Day 2)
startingPosition: Both seated, attacker in Single Leg X.

players.objective: Fulfill all three conditions, in any order, on both legs: cross the leg to the opposite side of the body, put feet to the inside between the partner's knees, and capture the second leg. Repeat all three on the other leg before losing connection.
players.winCondition: Complete all conditions on both legs.
constraints: Must maintain connection throughout

players.objective: Disconnect and free the leg at any time.

designRationale: By asking to do things that are not tactically optimized, it helps you get used to novel things.

title: Toe Capture + Hand Connection (B-Team Day 2)
startingPosition: Both seated, attacker in Single Leg X.

players.objective: Catch the partner's toes in the armpit, scoop under the heel, and connect hands. Do this on the straight side first, then transition to the cross side. Repeat on both legs without losing connection.
constraints: Feet positioning is free

players.objective: Free the leg or break all connections.

title: Progressive Finishing — Earn Your Starting Position (B-Team Day 2)
startingPosition: Inside entanglement, both legs controlled.

players.objective: Separate the partner's feet → capture toes → connect hands → finish (tap). If successful, the next round starts from single leg: get to cross-leg position with feet inside before finishing. If successful again, the next round starts from just inside position: entangle, get feet inside, cross leg, then finish.
constraints: Each failure resets to that failure point

players.objective: Pull the leg free at any time.

constraints: Each successful finish backs the attacker further out
designRationale: Every failed finish pushes you further from the finishing point — you must earn your way back.

title: Keep Them Down (B-Team Day 2)
startingPosition: Attacker with double feet inside, entanglement of choice.

players.objective: Entangle using any entanglement, catch the toes, and connect hands with a heel-hook finishing grip while the partner is on the ground. The full space may be used: stand if needed to keep the hips down. No finish is required.
players.winCondition: Fulfill grip conditions with partner grounded.

players.objective: Three options: standing + full disconnect, standing + one leg in between, OR standing + both legs outside.

designRationale: The most frustrating thing attacking legs — people getting up and coming off the mat.

title: Control the Entanglement (Inside Ashi)
startingPosition: Inside Ashi / Saddle / 411 / Cross Ashi — attacker has both feet inside, hooked to hip.

players.objective: Stay connected to the hip. Control the secondary leg. Collect the second leg if it escapes.
Free the knee line by hand fighting and pushing out. Use ballerina toes or karate/sidekick foot.
constraints: No floppy feet
Continuous — switch roles if nobody escapes

title: False Grip Hunt (Inside Ashi, One Hand)
startingPosition: Same as Control the Entanglement — Inside Ashi / Saddle.

players.objective: Same hip connection and secondary leg control. Can only use one arm to capture the heel.
players.winCondition: Establish a false grip on the heel.
constraints: Can only use one arm

players.objective: Same ballerina toe / karate foot. Hand fight to prevent the grip.

constraints: Stop when false grip is established — no submissions

title: Upgrade the Position (9010 / Outside Base Guard)
startingPosition: Outside base / 9010 — one foot outside, more rotation available but less control.

players.objective: Same rules — connect to hip, control secondary leg. Can now rotate around knee and attempt to expose heel.
Same foot positions.
players.winCondition: Clear the knee line and escape.

title: Upgrade Race (50/50)
startingPosition: 50/50 — open legs, no crossing/locking feet down.

players.objective: Upgrade position by getting closer to opponent's hip / coming across body. False grip on the heel if given. Defend the heel first, then work the upgrade.
players.winCondition: Either player: upgrade position OR false grip on heel.
constraints: Do not lock/cross feet — stay open and active
Do not lock/cross your feet — stay open and active

title: Hip Control Battle (Double Butt Scoot)
startingPosition: Double butt scoot — both seated, one in / one out, hands free.

players.objective: Hand fight and pummel to attach to a hip-to-hip leg entanglement.
constraints: Wrapping the knee doesn't count — must be hip
Wrapping the knee doesn't count — must be hip

title: Get Up (Double Butt Scoot + Stand)
startingPosition: Same as Hip Control Battle — double butt scoot.

players.objective: Same hip control battle. Added win condition: stand up and retrieve — if you can get to your feet and out, you win.
players.winCondition: Hip control OR stand up and out.
constraints: A player trying to stand must control the bottom leg; otherwise the other player gets up freely

designRationale: Entries to leg entanglements begin to emerge organically.

title: Three-Way (Hip / Stand / Back)
startingPosition: Same as Get Up — double butt scoot.

players.objective: Three win conditions: hip control, stand up and out, or get to opponent's back.
constraints: No demo — let it emerge
No demo — let it emerge

title: Saddle Heel Hide (Play to Win)
startingPosition: Attacker has defender in the saddle (cross ashi) with secondary leg controlled.

players.objective: Maintain saddle control with the secondary-leg grip. Dig for a false grip on the heel.
constraints: No ripping

players.objective: Use ballerina toe to hide the heel. Boot the foot on the attacker's hip. Free the trapped leg and re-hide the heel if recaptured. Spin or extract to escape.

designRationale: Start in the worst spot. Once you're comfortable in the worst spot, the other spots are not as scary.

title: Saddle → 90/10 Upgrade (Play to Win)
startingPosition: Saddle with secondary leg control.

players.objective: Foot to center/stomach, wrap around hip. Back heel to lock hip. Rotate around knee to reach 90/10. Dig for heel.
Hide heel, ballerina toe, extract secondary leg.

designRationale: Harder to spin out than from saddle.

title: 50/50 Shootout → 90/10 (Play to Win)
startingPosition: Open 50/50 — feet not crossed.

players.objective: Hide heel immediately. Battle to reach 80/20 → 90/10. Whoever gets upgrade first can dig for heel.
constraints: Do not lock/cross your feet — stay open and active
Do not lock/cross your feet — stay open and active
designRationale: Don't just lock up a triangle and stall. The person who is more aggressive and not worried wins this.

title: Double Butt Scoot — Leg Entanglement / Get Up (Play to Win)
startingPosition: Both seated, one inside, one outside.

players.objective: Option A: get to any leg entanglement — inside pummeling, no running away. Option B: first player to stand wins.
players.winCondition: Option A: reach entanglement. Option B: stand without being leg-locked.
constraints: No running away
Opponent can shoot for leg entries to prevent the standup
designRationale: Neutral entry game to reach any leg entanglement, or simply stand up.

title: Woj Control Without Submitting
startingPosition: Woj lock position.

players.objective: Establish and hold the Woj lock position without finishing. Focus on control only.

constraints: Underdeveloped — add rules and win conditions as needed

title: Woj with One Arm Controlled
startingPosition: Woj lock position with one of partner's arms already controlled.

players.objective: Same as Woj Control but with one of partner's arms already controlled.

constraints: Underdeveloped — add rules and win conditions as needed

title: Playing the Whole Space
source: Playing the Whole Space (Greg Souders Queretaro Seminar)
startingPosition: Bottom player supine, both feet between partner's knees, both hands on partner's ankles. Top player on the ground.

players.objective: Any of: reach any entanglement, get to feet and make partner's back touch mat without guard, OR lock hands around partner's hips.
Get to feet and break all connections.
players.winCondition: Get to feet and break all connections.

designRationale: No matter where we're going — as long as we can get access to our partner's ankles and keep it off the mat, we have access to the whole space.

title: Out to the Ankle
source: Playing the Whole Space (Greg Souders Queretaro Seminar)
startingPosition: Both players standing. Attacker gripping partner's leg at the knee.

players.objective: Precursor: slide grip from knee to ankle. Then (partner down first): entangle any leg, get hips, or make partner's back touch mat.
constraints: With new players, require hip to touch mat before entangling

players.objective: Free the leg. If defender falls, must get up with no connections.

constraints: With new players, require hip to touch mat before entangling to avoid knee injuries

title: Even Start
source: Playing the Whole Space (Greg Souders Queretaro Seminar)
startingPosition: Both players on the ground, each with one foot on the inside.

players.objective: Attack simultaneously — first to: separate and stand up, entangle and put partner down, lock hands around hips, or put partner's back on mat.
players.winCondition: First to any of the four.

designRationale: As long as we can get access to our partner's ankles and keep it off the mat, we have access to the whole space.

title: Hand Connection Denial — Standing (Behind)
source: Just Stand Up (Rob Cole - Ecopalooza Spring 2024)
startingPosition: Attacker behind defender, covering the knuckles.

players.objective: Connect hands around the waist, a leg, or anywhere from shoulders to ankles.
Get hips away and face the attacker.

title: Re-attack on the Break (Just Stand Up)
source: Just Stand Up (Rob Cole - Ecopalooza Spring 2024)
startingPosition: Same as Hand Connection Denial — attacker behind defender.

players.objective: Same hand connection logic, but on the break both players battle for hip control or a single leg.
Get hips away and face the attacker.

title: One Hand, One Knee Get-Up
source: Just Stand Up (Rob Cole - Ecopalooza Spring 2024)
startingPosition: Defender in quadruped — one hand, one knee on the mat.

players.objective: Get defender's hip to the mat OR both hands to the mat.
players.winCondition: Hip to mat OR both hands to mat.
constraints: Cannot connect hands

players.objective: Maintain the one-hand/one-knee base and get to both feet.

constraints: Attacker cannot connect hands

title: Referee Position / Turtle — Hip Breakdown
source: Just Stand Up (Rob Cole - Ecopalooza Spring 2024)
startingPosition: Defender in referee position (turtle). Attacker has any unconnected grip.

players.objective: Break defender to a hip, keep hips on the mat.
constraints: Cannot connect hands

players.objective: Keep getting back to turtle. Keep wrists clean.

constraints: Switch after a set time

title: Chest-to-Chest Get-Up (No Hands)
source: Just Stand Up (Rob Cole - Ecopalooza Spring 2024)
startingPosition: Defender on back, one shoulder off mat. Attacker chest-to-chest, no hands.

players.objective: Stay chest-to-chest or chest-to-back using only body weight and legs.
constraints: No hands (no connected grip)

players.objective: Get to both feet any way possible.

designRationale: Forces the attacker to use toes, chest pressure, and gravity — not arms. If controlling upper body, legs are free. If on lower body, head can come up.

title: Chest-to-Chest — With Free Grip
source: Just Stand Up (Rob Cole - Ecopalooza Spring 2024)
startingPosition: Same as No Hands but defender gets a free grip.

players.objective: Connect hands and hold down using chest, legs, arms.
Use the grip to break attachments and get up. Keep elbows to body.

designRationale: Focus of attention: Grip fighting — deny attachments while escaping.

title: Quarter Guard Pass → Pin
source: Just Stand Up (Rob Cole - Ecopalooza Spring 2024)
startingPosition: Attacker has crossface, underhook, and one knee trapped in quarter guard.

players.objective: Free the trapped knee, then pin shoulders to the mat (3-second count).
constraints: Can be backed up one step to half guard to increase difficulty

players.objective: Hold the knee, then if freed — try to get to turtle/feet.

title: Guard Connections + Stand-Up Option
source: Just Stand Up (Rob Cole - Ecopalooza Spring 2024)
startingPosition: Guard vs. passer — passer tries to break connections and reach the knee line.

players.objective: Break guard connections, cross the knee line.
Maintain connections AND has the option to stand up at any time.

designRationale: This emerged live during the session. Forces the top player to also monitor and prevent the stand-up, not just focus on passing.

title: Handfight to Closed Hands (Scaling)
startingPosition: Standing, hand fighting.

players.objective: Race to complete current level: L1: Close hands anywhere. L2: Close hands + put partner down. L3: Close hands → second connection → put partner down.
players.winCondition: Win = move on to next level. Lose = stay and repeat.

constraints: Each player tracks their own progression
designRationale: If you have different levels in the room, everybody needs something to work on.

title: Seated vs Standing (Scaling)
startingPosition: One player standing, one player seated.

players.objective: Constant goal: get past the feet to outside of legs and make shin touch the body.
L1: Make connection + destabilize. L2: Connection to hips (legs or hands only). L3: Either connection + make them fall.

constraints: Each player tracks their own progression

title: Completing Pins (Scaling)
startingPosition: Lying next to partner. Bottom on side facing top. Top's hands connected around bottom's waist.

players.objective: L1: Chest contact + hands under one elbow. L2: Get shoulders AND cover hips. L3: Start in half guard — connect, free leg, cover hips.
Same 3 ways all levels: guard recovery (knee in front), closed guard, or reversal/get up.

constraints: Each player tracks their own progression

title: Finishing (Scaling)
startingPosition: L1: Armlock breaking position. L2: Figure-four grip. L3: Under both elbows, top chooses position.

players.objective: L1: Hold down, separate hands, finish armlock. L2: Finish kimura OR take the figure four to any other submission. L3: Any submission; any body part, including legs, can be used under the elbows to stop them coming in.
L1: Pull arm free. L2: Pull arm free / break connection. L3: Pull both elbows in.

designRationale: We give the top player a role of collecting the head first before you finish.

title: Make Inside Connection (Fundamentals)
source: Standard Jiu Jitsu — CLA Class Games (White/Blue Belt)
startingPosition: Standing passer vs. Belly Up guard player.

players.objective: Get both feet to inside position and both hands on partner's legs. Hold as long as possible.
Prevent feet from reaching inside position. Stay close.

designRationale: The foundational function of the guard is to manage distance, and we can't do that unless we first make connections.

title: Make Inside Connection (One Leg at a Time)
source: Standard Jiu Jitsu — CLA Class Games (White/Blue Belt)
startingPosition: Standing passer vs. Belly Up guard player.

players.objective: Same goal but use one leg at a time. Reach out, hook, pull closer, then orient to inside position.
Same as Game 1.

constraints: Treat feet like hands — probe with one leg
designRationale: Students were reaching with both legs simultaneously, losing structure.

title: Destabilize to Hands / Advance to Knee Line
source: Standard Jiu Jitsu — CLA Class Games (White/Blue Belt)
startingPosition: Standing passer vs. Belly Up guard player.

players.objective: Make and maintain inside connection, then destabilize the top player onto their hands or butt. If the top player hits their butt, let them stand, restart; if they hit their hands, keep them there, continue pressure.
Clear the line of feet, advance to the knee line, and hold it.

designRationale: Once connection is established, the next layer is destabilization.

title: Side Control: Figure Four / Arm Extension / Exposed Back
source: Standard Jiu Jitsu — CLA Class Games (White/Blue Belt)
startingPosition: Side control (top vs. bottom).

players.objective: Achieve: figure four grip, arm extended, or chest-to-back with over-under grip.
Simply maintain pins and move between them.
Guard recovery or reversal.

constraints: Terminal — flip-flop and restart on success
designRationale: Context switch from guard work to pinning.

title: Rear Mount: Maintain Back / Clear Defenders
source: Standard Jiu Jitsu — CLA Class Games (White/Blue Belt)
startingPosition: Chest-to-back, hooks in, over-under grip.

players.objective: Maintain chest-to-back contact and over-under grip. Transition to side control if escaped.
Use hands to clear the defender's arms, then work toward strangulation. Legs may also be used for arm trapping.
Guard recovery or reversal.

constraints: Terminal — flip-flop and restart on success

title: Whole Game (Fundamentals)
source: Standard Jiu Jitsu — CLA Class Games (White/Blue Belt)
startingPosition: Belly Up guard vs. standing passer.

players.objective: Play full Jiu Jitsu: clear feet → knee line → chest-to-chest → figure four/arm extension/back → clear defenders → strangulation.

designRationale: Students have now played every component in isolation. This ties it together.

title: Breaking & Back Taking — Leg Entanglements
startingPosition: Any leg entanglement of choice.

players.objective: Finish a leg submission OR come up to take the back. Scaled: stay close, maintain hip attachment, search for both legs, capture toes.
Free the leg, counter submission, or pass the legs.

constraints: Continuous — flip-flop on win

title: Breaking & Back Taking — Arm (Figure-Four)
startingPosition: Bottom player on their side; top player with a figure-four grip on the arm.

players.objective: Submit OR take the back. Keep hips as close to the partner's shoulder as possible at all times. Separate the arm from everything it can touch (body, other arm, leg). Once separated, chain threats continuously (twisting lock → straight lock → strangle) with no lag time between threats.
Get free of threat and hide the back.

constraints: Continuous — flip-flop on win

title: Side Control — Hip Connection
startingPosition: Bottom player on their side; top player wrapping arm around partner's hip.

players.objective: Submit. Remove bottom player's hands. Search for underhooks — prioritize bottom arm underhook.
Seated open guard recovery, standing recovery, or reversal.

constraints: Continuous — flip-flop on win

title: All-Fours — Rear Hip Connection
startingPosition: Bottom player on all fours; top player connected around the waist from behind.

players.objective: Submit from any pin (chest-to-chest or chest-to-back). Always stay taller than the partner's back; never fall below their hip height. Break the partner off their base points progressively: feet → knees → hips / hands → elbows → shoulders.
Seated open guard, stand and turn to face, or reversal.

constraints: Continuous — flip-flop on win

title: Tournament Pinning
startingPosition: Side control.

players.objective: Get mount twice AND get back control (seatbelt and hooks).
Seated guard, standing, or sweep.

title: Tournament Pinning (with Submission)
startingPosition: Side control.

players.objective: Get mount twice AND get back control AND get a submission.
Seated guard, standing, or sweep.

title: Back Take from Hip Control
startingPosition: Top player on bottom player's hips.

players.objective: Take elbow off floor → get under elbow → chest-to-chest/chest-to-back → lock hands → cover hips with legs.
players.winCondition: Achieve back control with legs covering hips.

players.objective: Get to feet.

title: Guard Passing — Hips to Shoulders (Seminar Transcript)
startingPosition: Top player's hands locked around bottom player's hips.

players.objective: Change connection from hips → shoulders. Must secure hips first, then move to shoulders.
constraints: Must pass through hips first

players.objective: Get both feet on the floor with hands off the floor.
players.winCondition: Both feet on floor, no hands on mat.

constraints: Scaled by distance: start at hips, then knees, then feet
designRationale: Wrestlers come into grappling unable to hold people down. This game builds that.

title: Inside Position to Ankle Lock — No Releasing the Ankles
startingPosition: Seated with both feet inside hooking behind partner's knees, ankle grip on both legs.

players.objective: Entangle to outside ashi or SLX — without releasing ankle grips. Get an ankle lock.
constraints: Without releasing ankle grips

players.objective: Free the foot and get inside position.
players.winCondition: Free foot and get inside position.

constraints: Without releasing ankle grips

title: Standing Connection Wins
startingPosition: Both players standing; the transcript then says to start a leg across, but does not otherwise specify an exact initial connection.

players.objective: Create either a close rear-facing connection at the opponent's hips or shoulders while behind them, or a cross-leg/feet-inside entanglement with both legs collected. Do not go chest-to-chest.
players.winCondition: A close rear-facing hip/shoulder connection, or a cross-leg/feet-inside entanglement with both legs collected.
constraints: No chest-to-chest

players.objective: At minimum, stand up/get away and break all connections. A better result is a sweep, submission, back take, or reversal by getting behind the opponent.
players.winCondition: Minimum win: stand up/get away and break all connections. Better wins are a sweep, submission, back take, or reversal by getting behind the opponent.
constraints: If the defender ends on top, clear the legs to safety.
Top may not go chest-to-chest.
The defensive player must break all connections for the minimum win.
If the defensive player ends on top, clear the legs to safety.
Flip roles after every win.
designRationale: Transcript 2:41-5:23. The transcript gives two top wins (close rear-facing hip/shoulder connection, or cross-leg/feet-inside entanglement with both legs collected), a minimum defensive win, and a role flip after every win; the initial standing connection remains deliberately unspecified.

title: Bottom Offensive Connection
startingPosition: Bottom offensive player in any belly-up guard that is not an entanglement; single or double feet inside are allowed.

players.objective: Create cross-leg or cross-arm positioning, then connect hands to the opponent's center (hips or shoulders) while they are down, or get behind them with connected hands. Use connections to put the top player's hands on the ground and take opportunities to put them down and connect.
players.winCondition: Connected hands at the hips or shoulders while the opponent is down, or connected hands behind the opponent.

players.objective: Stay in the pocket and deny the bottom player's cross-leg/cross-arm and center-connection opportunities; passing is not required.
players.winCondition: Continuous defense: stay in the pocket and deny the bottom player's connection win; the transcript does not state a separate top scoring condition.
constraints: Stay in the pocket; the top player is not necessarily trying to pass.
The top player stays in the pocket and is not necessarily trying to pass.
Flip roles and positions after every win.
designRationale: Transcript 9:04-12:45. The bottom offensive player works from belly-up non-entanglement guard toward cross-leg/cross-arm and connected-center conditions. The transcript says the top stays in the pocket and is not necessarily trying to pass, so no separate top scoring condition is invented.

title: Six-Minute Connection Warm-Up
startingPosition: Both players start standing; play however you want, and sit if you do not want to wrestle.

players.objective: Play however you want and compete to connect to a leg off the ground, connect to the body front-facing or rear-facing, or make a shoulder/close-hand connection.
players.winCondition: Any of these connections counts: a leg connection off the ground, a body connection front-facing or rear-facing, or a shoulder/close-hand connection.

constraints: Six-minute warm-up round.
Find a new partner every round.
designRationale: Transcript 18:24-19:12. This is a six-minute connection warm-up with open play: players may sit, and the stated wins are a leg connection off the ground, front- or rear-facing body connection, or shoulder/close-hand connection.

title: Competition Score Rounds
startingPosition: Begin with the six-minute warm-up from standing. After each score, the scoring player chooses the next starting condition, such as neutral, guarded, or passing; the initial score-round start is not otherwise specified.

players.objective: Play first-to-score rounds: score a takedown, pass, back take, or submission. After scoring, choose the next starting condition.
players.winCondition: A takedown, pass, back take, or submission is a score; restart after each score. The scoring/winning player chooses the next start.

constraints: Do a six-minute connection warm-up first, starting standing; then run four 10-minute rounds.
Restart after every takedown, pass, back take, or submission score.
Only the scoring/winning player chooses the next start (neutral, guard, passing, or another option).
Find a new partner every round.
designRationale: Transcript 18:24-20:20. The first round is a six-minute standing connection warm-up, followed by four 10-minute first-to-score rounds. Every takedown, pass, back take, or submission restarts the round, and the scorer chooses the next start.
